pathway.title: Valvoline Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is the weakest dimension, and the credit case rests on reducing it. Net debt of USD 1,517.8 million is 2.79x Adjusted EBITDA, 0.29x above management's ceiling of 2.5x, and reported EBITDA gives 3.61x because it carries a USD 57.9 million loss on the forced sale of 45 acquired stores. Net debt is USD 125.0 million below the USD 1,642.8 million pro forma figure after the three quantified events that followed the fiscal 2025 balance sheet, so deleveraging has started; earnings include the acquired business for only seven of the twelve months, so the ratio overstates leverage by an amount the filings do not let us measure. Basis: calculation F6; calculation F15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11, 26, 30

Cash generation is improving but thin against the debt, and it depends on discretionary capital spending. Free cash flow of USD 140.5 million over the last twelve months converts 25.85% of Adjusted EBITDA and equals 8.77% of total debt, against 10.26% and 4.46% in fiscal 2025, and net debt is 10.80x last-twelve-months free cash flow. Capital expenditure absorbs 65.87% of operating cash flow, but 74.87% of nine-month capital spending is growth spending that management can defer, so free cash flow is closer to a policy choice than to a fixed charge. Basis: calculation F4; calculation F5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 29

Margins have held, but the cost pressure has not yet fully arrived. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27.34% in fiscal 2024, 27.29% in fiscal 2025 and 27.67% on the last twelve months, and gross margin fell by 1.00 percentage points to 39.46% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, almost all of it in other service delivery costs, while the materials ratio was flat at 16.53% and management says lubricant costs rose through the quarter and will stay elevated. Franchisee product prices generally follow base oil indices, while company-operated store prices are set by management, so a pricing lag would land on company-operated margin first: 1.00 percentage points of margin on last-twelve-months revenue is USD 19.64 million of Adjusted EBITDA and would lift net leverage to 2.90x. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F7; calculation F16; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19

Liquidity is the strongest dimension, but refinancing capacity cannot be fully assessed. Cash of USD 84.2 million and USD 470.1 million undrawn on the revolver give USD 554.3 million, 11.64 times the USD 47.6 million of installments printed for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027, while the last printed ladder shows USD 498.0 million in fiscal 2028 and USD 535.0 million after it and predates the Term Loan B. No maturity date is printed for the revolver or the term loans, and 67.00% of principal floats with no interest rate swaps since they matured in fiscal 2024, so a rise in base rates of 1.00 percentage points adds USD 10.86 million of annual interest. Basis: calculation F8; calculation F9; calculation F10; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 84, 97; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 29

Financial policy and governance are weak but improving. A material weakness in financial-reporting controls continues, the auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse at both earlier year-ends, and USD 1,850.2 million went to shareholders across fiscal 2023 to 2025; since the acquisition management has paused repurchases, prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A and lowered its leverage range to 1.5x to 2.5x. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, so no extraction channel is evidenced, but USD 325.0 million of repurchase authorization remains and the conditions for resuming it are not stated. Basis: calculation F13; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30, 31–34

The competitive position is average on the evidence supplied. Oil changes and related fees were 73.60% of nine-month revenue, 96.89% of fiscal 2025 revenue was earned in the United States, system-wide same-store sales grew 8.0% in the third quarter after 19 consecutive years of growth, and substantially all lubricants come from one supplier, so demand is durable but one service line, one country and one counterparty carry nearly all of it. The filings give no market share, so the strength of the brand against dealerships and other quick-lube chains is described by management, not measured. Basis: calculation F12; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18

The primary downside path is a margin squeeze followed by refinancing at higher leverage, not a liquidity shortfall. A 20% fall in Adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage to 3.49x and leave free cash flow positive before any spending cut, so liquidity holds, but the first debt wall and the revolver would then be refinanced above management's own range with two-thirds of the debt floating. Basis: calculation F7; calculation F8

runs.text: The ranked strengths are these. Maintenance-driven demand comes first: same-store sales growth of 8.0% in the third quarter and 19 consecutive years of growth give revenue visibility that lenders can rely on more than on discretionary retail. Liquidity of USD 554.3 million against USD 47.6 million of printed installments for the next two fiscal years comes second. Growth capital expenditure of USD 129.0 million in nine months is third, because it can be cut before any lender is affected. The stability of Adjusted EBITDA margin between 27.29% and 27.67% is fourth, and the paused repurchases and Term Loan A prepayment are fifth. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F5; calculation F9; calculation F10; calculation F13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 22

The ranked weaknesses are these. Net leverage of 2.79x above management's ceiling of 2.5x comes first, because every other risk is magnified by it. Concentration in one service line, one country and one lubricant supplier is second. The continuing material weakness in financial-reporting controls is third, since covenant and ratio calculations depend on reported figures. Thin debt service cover after capital spending, at 2.67x, and net debt of 10.80x free cash flow are fourth. A floating-rate share of 67.00% with no printed maturity dates for the revolver and term loans is fifth. Basis: calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F6; calculation F8; calculation F12

On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and market position is average and competitive advantage is average, because a branded network of company-operated and franchised stores in two countries supports the first, while competitors offer the same convenience proposition and no share is measured. Business diversification is weak: one segment, one country and one supplier. Cost and capex flexibility is average, helped by deferrable growth capital expenditure and a franchised half of the network, held back by a labour-intensive store cost base. Margin stability is average, with a stable adjusted margin and an unproven cost pass-through. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F5; calculation F12; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22

Free cash flow stability is weak, because free cash flow of USD 47.9 million in fiscal 2025 rose to USD 140.5 million only on the last twelve months and equals 4.46% to 8.77% of debt. Ability to refinance is average, supported by a Term Loan B that was placed in December 2025 and repriced down by 0.25 percentage points on June 30, 2026 and limited by an unrated, partly unknown maturity profile. Liquidity is strong over the next 12 months to 24 months for the reasons above. Financial policy and governance is weak but improving. The trend across the profile is stable operations with leverage that rose when the acquisition closed and has since fallen, and the missing data are covenant definitions, maturity dates, cash interest after the Term Loan B and any year-end figure after June 30, 2026. Basis: calculation F4; calculation F9; calculation F10; calculation F15; calculation F18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 29–30

runs.text: The transaction that defines the credit today is the acquisition of Breeze Autocare, an independent operator of quick lube stores in California, Texas and the Midwest, signed in February 2025 and closed on December 1, 2025 for USD 637.4 million of cash, with the Federal Trade Commission requiring the immediate sale of 45 acquired stores. The seller named in the annual report is Greenbriar; the buyer of the 45 stores named there is Mainstreet Auto, LLC. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 108–109; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11

The acquisition was funded by a new seven-year Term Loan B of USD 740.0 million added to the Senior Credit Agreement in December 2025, with the excess used to repay the revolver. On June 30, 2026 the Term Loan B was repriced to the adjusted term Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 1.750% from 2.000%, and Valvoline prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A in the third quarter. The 2031 notes of USD 535.0 million were not changed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 12; 10-Q_2025-12-31_vvv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

Earlier history shapes the structure: the former Global Products business was sold to Aramco Overseas Company B.V. on March 1, 2023 for net proceeds of USD 2,383 million, leaving a supply agreement, a shared brand agreement and indemnities with the buyer's business and with Ashland. Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_vvv-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 19, 37–38

fields.value: The five Valvoline filings support a credit snapshot as at June 30, 2026, not later: debt, cash and revolver availability are usable, but covenant headroom and the maturity schedule after the 2025 term loan are not. The latest balance sheet is 141 days before the as-of date, and the fiscal 2026 annual report, executed credit documents, ratings, market prices and peer data are absent. Management's leverage target also moved without explanation, from 2.5x to 3.5x in the December 2025 report to 1.5x to 2.5x in the March 2026 report. Otherwise the filings suffice for the three requested analyses, each within the limits stated here.

fields.value: **Executed credit documents not supplied (material).** The executed Senior Credit Agreement, the December 2025 amendment that added the seven-year Term Loan B of USD 740.0 million, the June 30, 2026 repricing amendment and the indenture for the 2031 Notes are not supplied, and the run settings declare no legal documents. The financial covenants are known only from the summary in the fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 annual reports: a maximum net leverage ratio of 4.5x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.0x, tested each fiscal quarter. No supplied text restates the levels after the two amendments, defines net debt or Adjusted EBITDA for covenant purposes, or prints a step-down or cure right, so covenant headroom is not established. The only evidence is management's statement that it complied with all covenants at June 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Control weakness over financial reporting (material).** Management reports that a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting, in the design of business process controls, persisted at June 30, 2026, that disclosure controls were not effective, and that it expects remediation during fiscal 2026. The auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse at September 30, 2025 and at September 30, 2024, while its opinions on the financial statements state that they present fairly, and management reports no identified material misstatement. The quarterly statements are unaudited, and the acquired Breeze business, about 8% of nine-month net revenues and about 20% of total assets, is excluded from management's fiscal 2026 assessment. Figures from these filings are usable but carry a reliability qualification until remediation is shown.

fields.value: **Maturity schedule and lease balances after the 2025 amendments not printed (minor).** The latest debt maturity table is at September 30, 2025, before the Term Loan B: USD 23.8 million in fiscal 2026, USD 23.8 million in fiscal 2027, USD 498.0 million in fiscal 2028 and USD 535.0 million thereafter. The quarterly reports print no maturity table and do not state the maturity dates of the Term Loan B (a seven-year facility), the Term Loan A or the revolver, so the maturity wall at June 30, 2026 is not established. Finance lease liabilities, which sit outside total debt, were USD 244.5 million at September 30, 2025 and are not printed for June 30, 2026. No supplied filing mentions purchase commitments, factoring or supplier finance.

fields.value: **Ratings, market data, peers and outlook not supplied (minor).** No credit rating, rating-agency comment, bond or loan price, spread, peer set, earnings release or call transcript is supplied, and the run settings carry none. A search of all five filings for rating-agency names and for guidance or outlook found no numerical earnings or cash flow guidance beyond a fiscal 2026 capital expenditure forecast of USD 250 million to USD 280 million in the fiscal 2025 annual report. The June 2026 report says share repurchases resume on achievement of commitments established at the time of the acquisition, but no supplied document sets those commitments out. The only market-based figure for the debt is the fair value of the 2031 Notes, USD 492.6 million at June 30, 2026 against a carrying value of USD 531.5 million.

fields.value: **Board, ownership and compensation not supplied (minor).** Directors, executive compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party information are incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not supplied. The fiscal 2025 annual report lists the executive officers as of November 18, 2025. The run settings name no sponsor, parent or guarantor, so ownership and governance beyond the officer list are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Differing figures and targets between reports (minor).** The pre-tax gain on the sale of 10 company-operated stores to a franchisee in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 is USD 14.8 million in the quarter to December 31, 2025 and in the six months to March 31, 2026, but USD 14.3 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026, a difference of USD 0.5 million. The prior-year gain on the 39-store sale moves from USD 73.9 million to USD 74.2 million to USD 74.3 million over the same three reports. Separately, the fiscal 2025 annual report expected the Breeze acquisition to cover 207 stores for a net purchase price of USD 593 million, subject to adjustments, while the June 2026 report gives cash consideration of USD 637.4 million and says the acquisition initially included 204 stores; neither report reconciles the two. Management's leverage target also changes: both annual reports and the December 2025 quarterly report describe a ratings agency target adjusted EBITDA net leverage ratio of 2.5x to 3.5x, while the March and June 2026 quarterly reports give a net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of 1.5x to 2.5x, so the two targets are not on one stated definition. No filing explains these changes. The quarterly reports also state that certain prior period amounts were reclassified, so prior-year comparatives may differ from the original fiscal 2025 annual report. The June 2026 figures are the latest and are used as the current reading.

It would carry more weight if fiscal 2026 year-end figures show net debt below USD 1,517.8 million without further acquisitions, and it carries less weight because the other assets and liabilities line turned from an outflow of USD 0.2 million to an inflow of USD 42.6 million.

fields.value: **Interim cash interest paid is not printed (High).** The nine-month cash flow statements print no interest paid, so Cash Interest Paid is not supplied for the nine months to June 30, 2026 and the nine months to June 30, 2025. EBITDA to cash interest at June 30, 2026 is therefore not calculable, and the interest cover charts stop at fiscal 2025 year-end, before the Term Loan B raised debt. Closing the gap needs interest paid for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 or the fiscal 2026 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **No statements after June 30, 2026 (High).** Every balance and the last-twelve-months construction end at June 30, 2026. Year-end fiscal 2026 debt, cash, EBITDA and cash interest are not available, and the pro forma table covers only events after the fiscal 2025 balance sheet. Closing the gap needs the fiscal 2026 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Maturity dates and the maturity wall after the Term Loan B are not printed (Medium).** The only maturity ladder is at September 30, 2025, with fiscal 2029 and fiscal 2030 printed as dashes that the printed total shows to be nil. No report prints the maturity date of the Term Loan A, the Term Loan B or the revolver, or a ladder after the December 2025 amendment, so the maturity wall at June 30, 2026 is not established and the fiscal 2031 bucket is placed by Analyst Judgement. Closing the gap needs the executed credit agreement and its amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Carrying values by instrument are not printed (Medium).** Only the 2031 Notes' carrying value is printed, so the Term Loan A and Term Loan B carry principal in the instrument register and the remaining issuance costs and discounts of USD 15.5 million are one adjustment row. The gross debt used in every ratio is the printed total and is not affected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Finance lease liabilities at June 30, 2026 are not printed (Medium).** Finance lease liabilities were USD 244.5 million at September 30, 2025 and sit outside total debt; the June 2026 report prints only the amounts assumed with Breeze Autocare, so the current total is not established and any lease-adjusted leverage cannot be built. Closing the gap needs the lease note of the fiscal 2026 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Last-twelve-months EBITDA excludes Breeze Autocare before December 1, 2025 (Medium).** No pro forma EBITDA for the acquisition is printed, so leverage at June 30, 2026 is stated on earnings that include the acquired business for seven months of the twelve and the debt that funded it in full. The ratio overstates leverage against a full-year basis by an amount that is not established. Closing the gap needs a pro forma EBITDA from the issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Adjusted EBITDA key items are defined differently across periods (Medium).** The fiscal 2026 key items include amortization of Breeze acquired intangibles and temporary financing costs, and the information technology label now includes control remediation costs; the last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 543.5 million mixes the two definitions and the effect is not quantified in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Covenant definitions are not supplied (Medium).** The financial covenants are summarised in the fiscal 2025 annual report as a maximum net leverage ratio of 4.5x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.0x, tested each quarter, and the company states compliance at June 30, 2026. The covenant definitions of net debt and Adjusted EBITDA are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not inferred or calculated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Security, rank, margins and floors for the loans are partly not stated (Medium).** The security and legal rank of the Term Loan B are taken from the Senior Credit Agreement it amends as Analyst Judgement, because no filing after the amendment restates them. The margins in force at June 30, 2026 for the Term Loan A and the revolver, and any floors, are not stated. The debt stack therefore ranks the three facilities equally.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Interim cash flow lines and dash entries are not supplied (Low).** The interim statements do not print deferred income taxes, pension remeasurement, purchases and proceeds of investments, finance lease payments or income taxes paid, so those cells are not supplied for the nine-month columns. Entries printed as a dash are not read as zero: the loss on extinguishment of debt in fiscal 2025, operating cash flows from discontinued operations and repurchases of common stock in the nine months to June 30, 2026, and the exchange effect on cash in fiscal 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Total liabilities and the 2025-06-30 balance sheet are not printed (Low).** The balance sheets print no total liabilities line, so it is calculated and shown as such, and the June 2026 report prints no balance sheet at June 30, 2025, so net debt at that date and a prior-year last-twelve-months leverage are not available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **No segment revenue schedule applies (Low).** The issuer reports one segment, so no segment revenue or elimination rows exist and no segment sum is stated; revenue by service category is printed in the quarterly report but is not a segment schedule.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Some period-end store counts and event amounts are not printed (Low).** Company-operated and franchised store counts for fiscal 2024 are not printed in the text of the fiscal 2024 report. The proceeds of the October 2025 sale of 10 stores are not stated, so the post-balance-sheet table leaves that row unquantified, and the dates of the 21 other store acquisitions are given only as the nine months to June 30, 2026.

Fiscal 2024 figures here follow the later report.

fields.value: Business & governance for Valvoline Inc (issuer vvv-1674910), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, operating model, ownership, transactions, governance and capital allocation from the five supplied filings, with every gap stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valvoline's operating model is resilient, but creditors now hold claims on an acquisitive, more leveraged issuer: nineteen years of same-store sales growth support cash flow, while a debt-funded acquisition, reliance on one lubricant supplier and a continuing control weakness add event and reporting risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nearly half of third-quarter revenue growth came from the acquisition: Breeze Autocare added USD 50.8 million of the USD 105.6 million increase. No sponsor or controlling shareholder is named in the supplied filings and the company pays no dividend and does not expect to, which limits extraction risk, but board and ownership detail is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a durable, low-ticket maintenance service. Oil changes and related fees were 73.60% of nine-month revenue, other maintenance services 21.26% and franchise fees 5.14%, and system-wide same-store sales grew 8.0% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 after 19 consecutive years of growth through fiscal 2025, so demand follows vehicle maintenance needs rather than discretionary spending. Management characterises the network's record as operational excellence; the figures show growth, not the reason for it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth now leans heavily on a debt-funded acquisition. Breeze Autocare closed on December 1, 2025 for USD 637.4 million of cash, funded by a USD 740.0 million Term Loan B, and contributed 7.75% of nine-month revenue; the required sale of 45 acquired stores cost a USD 57.9 million pre-tax loss. The mechanism is higher debt service against earnings that include the acquired stores for only part of the period, which is why creditors should read current leverage together with the Financial foundation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are under cost pressure that is not yet labour or materials. Gross margin fell by 1.00 percentage points to 39.46% in the third quarter, and most of the decline sits in other service delivery costs, which rose from 19.68% to 20.62% of revenue while labour and materials ratios were flat; management adds that lubricant costs rose through the quarter and are expected to stay elevated. A pricing lag against a single supplier's costs would hit margin next.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19, 22–23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supply is concentrated in one counterparty. The stores buy substantially all lubricants from the owner of the former Global Products business under a long-term supply agreement, and the brand is shared with that owner; any interruption, quality failure or dispute would reach every company-operated store and the franchisees' product supply at once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance evidence is thin and its main risk is control reliability. Management reports a material weakness in internal control that began with the 2024 system implementation and persisted at June 30, 2026, the auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse at both prior year-ends, and the acquired business is excluded from the fiscal 2026 assessment, so the reliability of reported figures depends on remediation that management expects during fiscal 2026. The chief financial officer changed in May 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation was shareholder-led before the acquisition and is creditor-friendly after it. Share repurchases and dividends totalled USD 1,850.2 million across fiscal 2023 to 2025, after the Global Products sale brought in USD 2,383 million, while management has since paused repurchases, prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A and lowered its leverage target. The shift is documented but untested by a fiscal 2026 year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is momentum and deleveraging: same-store sales growth of 8.0% in the third quarter, free cash flow of USD 112.3 million in the nine months, a USD 50.0 million prepayment of the Term Loan A, and a franchised half of the network (49.84% of stores) that adds fee income without store capital. The view would improve if the fiscal 2026 year-end shows net leverage inside management's target range, remediation of the control weakness is declared complete, and no further debt-funded acquisition is announced; it would worsen if a gap opens between lubricant costs and pricing or the supply relationship is disrupted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Directors, compensation and shareholder detail sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the governance view rests on officers and filings and could move to lower risk if the proxy shows independent oversight of the control remediation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction that defines the credit today is the acquisition of Breeze Autocare, an independent operator of quick lube stores in California, Texas and the Midwest, signed in February 2025 and closed on December 1, 2025 for USD 637.4 million of cash, with the Federal Trade Commission requiring the immediate sale of 45 acquired stores. The seller named in the annual report is Greenbriar; the buyer of the 45 stores named there is Mainstreet Auto, LLC.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition was funded by a new seven-year Term Loan B of USD 740.0 million added to the Senior Credit Agreement in December 2025, with the excess used to repay the revolver. On June 30, 2026 the Term Loan B was repriced to the adjusted term Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 1.750% from 2.000%, and Valvoline prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A in the third quarter. The 2031 notes of USD 535.0 million were not changed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier history shapes the structure: the former Global Products business was sold to Aramco Overseas Company B.V. on March 1, 2023 for net proceeds of USD 2,383 million, leaving a supply agreement, a shared brand agreement and indemnities with the buyer's business and with Ashland.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Valvoline Inc (issuer vvv-1674910), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated credit view of the business, cash flow, leverage, liquidity, refinancing, governance and downside path from the five supplied filings and the three earlier analyses, with every gap stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valvoline's credit profile is adequate: a cash-generative maintenance-service business now carries more debt than management's own ceiling allows, so creditors depend on free cash flow to reduce leverage rather than on any cushion in the capital structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F6; calculation F4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 1,517.8 million is 2.79x Adjusted EBITDA against a stated ceiling of 2.5x, but liquidity of USD 554.3 million, nine-month free cash flow of USD 112.3 million and growth capital expenditure of USD 129.0 million that can be deferred make near-term liquidity distress unlikely on the evidence supplied. The primary path to deterioration is a lubricant cost squeeze or a fall in maintenance demand that arrives while the control weakness, the unknown maturity of the term loans and a floating-rate share of 67.00% remain unresolved.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F6; calculation F8; calculation F10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 19, 29–30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the weakest dimension, and the credit case rests on reducing it. Net debt of USD 1,517.8 million is 2.79x Adjusted EBITDA, 0.29x above management's ceiling of 2.5x, and reported EBITDA gives 3.61x because it carries a USD 57.9 million loss on the forced sale of 45 acquired stores. Net debt is USD 125.0 million below the USD 1,642.8 million pro forma figure after the three quantified events that followed the fiscal 2025 balance sheet, so deleveraging has started; earnings include the acquired business for only seven of the twelve months, so the ratio overstates leverage by an amount the filings do not let us measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F6; calculation F15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11, 26, 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is improving but thin against the debt, and it depends on discretionary capital spending. Free cash flow of USD 140.5 million over the last twelve months converts 25.85% of Adjusted EBITDA and equals 8.77% of total debt, against 10.26% and 4.46% in fiscal 2025, and net debt is 10.80x last-twelve-months free cash flow. Capital expenditure absorbs 65.87% of operating cash flow, but 74.87% of nine-month capital spending is growth spending that management can defer, so free cash flow is closer to a policy choice than to a fixed charge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F4; calculation F5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have held, but the cost pressure has not yet fully arrived. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27.34% in fiscal 2024, 27.29% in fiscal 2025 and 27.67% on the last twelve months, and gross margin fell by 1.00 percentage points to 39.46% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, almost all of it in other service delivery costs, while the materials ratio was flat at 16.53% and management says lubricant costs rose through the quarter and will stay elevated. Franchisee product prices generally follow base oil indices, while company-operated store prices are set by management, so a pricing lag would land on company-operated margin first: 1.00 percentage points of margin on last-twelve-months revenue is USD 19.64 million of Adjusted EBITDA and would lift net leverage to 2.90x.

fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F7; calculation F16; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the strongest dimension, but refinancing capacity cannot be fully assessed. Cash of USD 84.2 million and USD 470.1 million undrawn on the revolver give USD 554.3 million, 11.64 times the USD 47.6 million of installments printed for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027, while the last printed ladder shows USD 498.0 million in fiscal 2028 and USD 535.0 million after it and predates the Term Loan B. No maturity date is printed for the revolver or the term loans, and 67.00% of principal floats with no interest rate swaps since they matured in fiscal 2024, so a rise in base rates of 1.00 percentage points adds USD 10.86 million of annual interest.

fields.value: Financial policy and governance are weak but improving. A material weakness in financial-reporting controls continues, the auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse at both earlier year-ends, and USD 1,850.2 million went to shareholders across fiscal 2023 to 2025; since the acquisition management has paused repurchases, prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A and lowered its leverage range to 1.5x to 2.5x. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, so no extraction channel is evidenced, but USD 325.0 million of repurchase authorization remains and the conditions for resuming it are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F13; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30, 31–34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The competitive position is average on the evidence supplied. Oil changes and related fees were 73.60% of nine-month revenue, 96.89% of fiscal 2025 revenue was earned in the United States, system-wide same-store sales grew 8.0% in the third quarter after 19 consecutive years of growth, and substantially all lubricants come from one supplier, so demand is durable but one service line, one country and one counterparty carry nearly all of it. The filings give no market share, so the strength of the brand against dealerships and other quick-lube chains is described by management, not measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a margin squeeze followed by refinancing at higher leverage, not a liquidity shortfall. A 20% fall in Adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage to 3.49x and leave free cash flow positive before any spending cut, so liquidity holds, but the first debt wall and the revolver would then be refinanced above management's own range with two-thirds of the debt floating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that deleveraging is already visible and leverage is overstated. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27.37% against 26.80% a year earlier, free cash flow was USD 112.3 million against USD 19.7 million, USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A was prepaid, and the reported ratio carries a USD 57.9 million forced-sale loss and only seven months of Breeze Autocare earnings. Reaching the 2.5x ceiling at today's earnings needs net debt USD 159.05 million lower, which compares with the USD 125.0 million of reduction since the acquisition, or Adjusted EBITDA of USD 607.12 million at today's net debt, and the filings do not quantify the acquired earnings still missing from the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F4; calculation F6; calculation F15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 12, 26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the fiscal 2026 annual report shows net leverage inside the 2.5x ceiling without another debt-funded acquisition, the control weakness is declared remediated, and the maturity dates show no wall inside 24 months. It would worsen if lubricant costs outrun price increases for two quarters, same-store sales growth turns negative, repurchases resume while leverage is above 2.5x, or the revolver proves to mature before the fiscal 2028 bucket.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Market share and competitor financial data are not supplied, so the finding that the competitive position is average rests on management's description and the same-store sales record; a measured share lead would move the assessment toward strong, and a share loss in company-operated markets would move it toward weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The interim cash flow statements print no interest paid, so debt service capacity after the Term Loan B is judged on an expense-based cover of 5.32x and on capital-expenditure-adjusted cover of 2.67x rather than on cash interest; a cash figure materially above the expense would lower the cash-flow durability view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F3; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity dates of the revolver and the term loans are not printed and the last ladder predates the Term Loan B, so the view that the first large maturity is the fiscal 2028 bucket is the last printed position and not a current one; a revolver maturing earlier would bring the refinancing risk forward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement's covenant definitions are not supplied, so the stated maximum net leverage of 4.5x cannot be applied to the figures used here and no covenant headroom is concluded; the view that liquidity distress is unlikely assumes the company stays in compliance, as it states it does.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating or agency opinion is supplied, so the nine-dimension assessments are the analyst's own and cannot be compared with a rating, and the view on market access rests on the Term Loan B having been placed and repriced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No statement after June 30, 2026 is supplied, so every conclusion on leverage and deleveraging describes the position at June 30, 2026; a fiscal 2026 year-end net debt figure that differs from USD 1,517.8 million would change the leverage finding directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ranked strengths are these. Maintenance-driven demand comes first: same-store sales growth of 8.0% in the third quarter and 19 consecutive years of growth give revenue visibility that lenders can rely on more than on discretionary retail. Liquidity of USD 554.3 million against USD 47.6 million of printed installments for the next two fiscal years comes second. Growth capital expenditure of USD 129.0 million in nine months is third, because it can be cut before any lender is affected. The stability of Adjusted EBITDA margin between 27.29% and 27.67% is fourth, and the paused repurchases and Term Loan A prepayment are fifth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F5; calculation F9; calculation F10; calculation F13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ranked weaknesses are these. Net leverage of 2.79x above management's ceiling of 2.5x comes first, because every other risk is magnified by it. Concentration in one service line, one country and one lubricant supplier is second. The continuing material weakness in financial-reporting controls is third, since covenant and ratio calculations depend on reported figures. Thin debt service cover after capital spending, at 2.67x, and net debt of 10.80x free cash flow are fourth. A floating-rate share of 67.00% with no printed maturity dates for the revolver and term loans is fifth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F6; calculation F8; calculation F12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and market position is average and competitive advantage is average, because a branded network of company-operated and franchised stores in two countries supports the first, while competitors offer the same convenience proposition and no share is measured. Business diversification is weak: one segment, one country and one supplier. Cost and capex flexibility is average, helped by deferrable growth capital expenditure and a franchised half of the network, held back by a labour-intensive store cost base. Margin stability is average, with a stable adjusted margin and an unproven cost pass-through.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F5; calculation F12; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is weak, because free cash flow of USD 47.9 million in fiscal 2025 rose to USD 140.5 million only on the last twelve months and equals 4.46% to 8.77% of debt. Ability to refinance is average, supported by a Term Loan B that was placed in December 2025 and repriced down by 0.25 percentage points on June 30, 2026 and limited by an unrated, partly unknown maturity profile. Liquidity is strong over the next 12 months to 24 months for the reasons above. Financial policy and governance is weak but improving. The trend across the profile is stable operations with leverage that rose when the acquisition closed and has since fallen, and the missing data are covenant definitions, maturity dates, cash interest after the Term Loan B and any year-end figure after June 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business model supports cash-flow visibility because revenue comes from low-ticket preventive maintenance tied to vehicle use, but it concentrates that visibility in a single service line. Oil changes and related fees were 73.60% of nine-month revenue, other maintenance services 21.26% and franchise fees 5.14%, and 96.89% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the United States. Stores are 49.84% franchised, so about half of the network pays fees on its sales without drawing on the issuer's capital; the risk mechanic is that royalties and product margin on franchised stores depend on franchisee sales and financing, which the annual report identifies as a dependency. The credit implication is steady, fee-supported cash flow with a narrow base, and a refinancing story that leans on the record of same-store sales growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is dispersed and no sponsor or controlling shareholder is named, so the credit risk is the willingness of management, not an owner's extraction. The company paid no dividend in fiscal 2024 or fiscal 2025 and does not expect to, but returned USD 1,850.2 million through repurchases and dividends across fiscal 2023 to 2025 after the Global Products sale, and then used a USD 740.0 million Term Loan B to fund a USD 637.4 million acquisition. The mechanic is that policy has moved from returning capital to adding debt for growth; the implication is that creditors should treat the paused repurchases and the lowered range of 1.5x to 2.5x as a commitment still to be proven, because USD 325.0 million of authorization remains and the resumption conditions are not set out. Guarantees of leases and franchisee debt add USD 105.8 million outside reported debt.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring and mostly non-discretionary, but pricing power is untested at the margin. Net revenues grew 5.64% in fiscal 2025, 20.19% in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 and 24.05% in the third quarter, where USD 50.8 million of the USD 105.6 million increase came from the acquired business, while system-wide same-store sales grew 8.0% with higher volumes and favourable pricing and service mix. The mechanic is that a customer can defer an oil change in a downturn or as miles driven fall, which the annual report lists as a risk, so durability rests on the company's ability to hold volume as prices rise. The implication is that revenue is predictable in normal conditions and cyclical at the margin, with no customer concentration measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F2; calculation F11; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9, 18–19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience rests on pass-through to franchisees and pricing action in company-operated stores, against a cost base of labour, materials and other service delivery costs. Labour was 24.29% of revenue and materials 17.39% in fiscal 2025, and in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 other service delivery costs rose to 20.62% of revenue from 19.68% while labour and materials were flat. The mechanic is operating leverage on store labour and a supplier whose prices follow base oil; the implication is that a sustained cost squeeze would reach Adjusted EBITDA before it reaches liquidity, and that wage legislation or tariffs, which the annual report flags, would add to it.

fields.value: Basis: calculation F16; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 21, 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high and mostly discretionary, which is the main source of flexibility in the credit. Capital expenditure was 13.81% of last-twelve-months revenue, USD 172.3 million in nine months of which USD 129.0 million was growth spending, and the company forecasts USD 250 million to USD 280 million for fiscal 2026. The mechanic is that growth spending, store development and acquisitions compete with debt reduction for the same operating cash flow. The implication is that free cash flow converts 25.85% of Adjusted EBITDA now, against 10.26% in fiscal 2025, and would rise by the amount of growth spending management chooses to defer; interim working-capital swings of USD 42.6 million in other assets and liabilities mean part of the improvement may not repeat.

fields.value: Basis: calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 28–29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is the force that matters most for margin: the market is fragmented and Valvoline competes with dealerships, repair centers and other quick-lube chains on brand, price, speed and location, so it can pass on cost but not earn above-cost pricing everywhere. Buyer power appears high because the filings show no switching cost for a consumer and give no measure of fleet or franchisee concentration; the largest franchisees add concentration risk to the royalty stream. Supplier power is high: substantially all lubricants come from one counterparty under a long-term agreement whose terms are not supplied. Substitutes are limited today, but electric vehicles and longer drain intervals, and owners who maintain their own vehicles, reduce visits over time. New entrants face the cost of real estate and brand building, which limits their effect on credit within the horizon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic and technology factors affect credit; regulation matters mainly through the franchise and acquisition rules. A recession or higher energy prices reduce miles driven and lead customers to defer maintenance, which would lower same-store sales and operating leverage on store labour; vehicle technology and manufacturer service intervals change drain frequency over a longer horizon. Federal Trade Commission review forced the sale of 45 acquired stores at a USD 57.9 million pre-tax loss, which shows that further consolidation by acquisition is constrained in a fragmented market with limited targets remaining, and wage and tariff changes pass through to costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: recurring maintenance demand and a same-store sales record of 19 years; liquidity of USD 554.3 million; a franchised half of the network that earns fees on sales; deferrable growth capital expenditure of USD 129.0 million in nine months; Adjusted EBITDA margin between 27.29% and 27.67% across three periods.

fields.value: - Weaknesses: net leverage of 2.79x above management's ceiling of 2.5x; one service line, one country and one lubricant supplier; a continuing material weakness in control; thin debt service cover of 2.67x after capital spending; 67.00% of principal at floating rates.

fields.value: - Opportunities that would improve credit quality: net debt falling by USD 159.05 million at today's earnings, which would bring leverage to the ceiling of 2.5x; repayment of the Term Loan A and revolver from free cash flow; and remediation of the control weakness, which management expects during fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threats that would weaken credit quality: lubricant costs that outrun pricing; resumption of repurchases while leverage is above the ceiling; a further debt-funded acquisition; and a maturity wall or revolver expiry that falls before refinancing conditions are known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 months to 24 months the outlook is for continued revenue growth and gradual deleveraging, with margin as the swing factor. The tailwinds are same-store sales growth of 8.0%, a full year of Breeze Autocare earnings from fiscal 2027, a USD 1.85 million annual interest saving from the Term Loan B repricing, and paused repurchases; the headwinds are lubricant costs management expects to stay elevated, interest expense that rose 37.97% from fiscal 2025 to the last twelve months, and integration and control remediation work. Over three to five years the support is network growth and franchise expansion, and the pressure comes from electric vehicle adoption and longer service intervals, the supplier relationship, and the refinancing of the fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2031 buckets, which together were 95.60% of principal at September 30, 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F9; calculation F17; calculation F18; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 18–19, 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a cost and demand squeeze that starts in company-operated store margin and ends in a refinancing at higher leverage. The initiating condition is that lubricant costs, which management expects to stay elevated, rise faster than prices at the same time as an economic slowdown or higher energy prices lead customers to defer oil changes. The first operational break is gross margin: the fall of 1.00 percentage points already seen in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 is worth USD 19.64 million of Adjusted EBITDA over a year of revenue, and fewer vehicles served per day would add to it through operating leverage on store labour. The financial transmission is arithmetic on net debt of USD 1,517.8 million: a 10% fall in Adjusted EBITDA lifts net leverage from 2.79x to 3.10x and a 20% fall to 3.49x, expense-based cover falls from 5.32x to 4.79x and 4.26x, and free cash flow before any tax relief falls from USD 140.5 million to USD 86.15 million and USD 31.80 million, still positive before any cut in growth spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F7; calculation F4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity holds under this path: USD 554.3 million of liquidity compares with USD 47.6 million of installments printed for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 and an undrawn revolver. The consequence arrives at refinancing, where the fiscal 2028 bucket and the revolver would be refinanced at leverage nearer 3.5x than the ceiling of 2.5x, with 67.00% of principal floating, so a rise in base rates of 1.00 percentage points adds USD 10.86 million of annual interest. Management's levers are to defer the USD 129.0 million of nine-month growth spending, keep repurchases paused, slow acquisitions and refranchise stores. They appear sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall over the next 12 months to 24 months but not to return leverage to the range without a recovery in earnings. The observable triggers are gross margin below 39.46% in consecutive quarters, same-store sales growth turning negative and net leverage rising above 2.79x. The sensitivities are Analyst Judgement arithmetic, not forecasts, and the covenant tests cannot be applied because their definitions are not supplied.

fields.value: Basis: calculation F5; calculation F7; calculation F8; calculation F10; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 29–30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Valvoline presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring maintenance demand, a franchised half of the network and deferrable growth capital expenditure, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 2.79x above management's ceiling of 2.5x, concentration in one service line, one country and one supplier, and a continuing control weakness. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.67% that has been stable across three periods and free cash flow of USD 140.5 million over the last twelve months, which is thin against net debt at 10.80x. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the maturity dates of the revolver and term loans, on the control remediation and on whether leverage reaches the ceiling before the fiscal 2028 bucket falls due. The primary downside path is a lubricant cost squeeze or a demand slowdown that raises leverage toward 3.5x with two-thirds of the debt floating.
